title: Inclusive Credit Risk Analytics Bolivia
subtitle: Responsible credit-portfolio analytics for monitoring growth, financial inclusion, branch performance, risk, forecasting and stress scenarios in Bolivia.
description: Branch-level credit portfolio analytics for monitoring growth, financial inclusion, risk, forecasting and stress scenarios in Bolivia through a reproducible decision-support workflow.
executive_summary: Operational Excel workbooks are transformed into a branch-level monthly analytical panel.
The public project presents aggregated portfolio, client, delinquency, inclusion, forecasting and stress-test outputs.
The analysis is descriptive and decision-support oriented; it does not claim causal poverty or welfare effects.
key_findings: The global active portfolio increased from 109.8 kBOB to 69,850.2 kBOB during the observed period.
Client outreach expanded from 18 to 3,827 clients.
Client distribution became more balanced between the two branches.
ARIMA is the selected global forecasting model by holdout RMSE among existing model outputs.
Stress scenarios help monitor resilience under documented assumptions without guaranteeing future performance.

dashboard.status: Reused existing GitHub Pages dashboard content

figures.title: Client growth
figures.alt: Client growth and credit depth figure

data_sources: Raw operational Excel workbooks kept outside public distribution.
Branch-level monthly analytical panel generated by the existing R workflow.
Public products use aggregate or branch-level outputs only.
methodology: Portfolio, inclusion, concentration and territorial balance KPIs.
Holdout validation for Naive, ETS and ARIMA models.
limitations: Operational branch-level data with limited period coverage.
No causal poverty, household welfare or firm productivity effects are estimated.
Forecasts support monitoring and do not guarantee future portfolio performance.
Stress tests represent documented scenarios rather than predictions.
Financial inclusion indicators are operational proxies.
reproducibility: Required packages are documented in the README.
Raw Excel workbooks are private and ignored from public Git tracking.
Public outputs are aggregated figures, tables, reports and dashboard files.
